app.name: Judgium
app.tagline: Every challenge conveyed fairly — where projects and judging meet.
app.description: Judgium is a judging platform that connects everything from hackathon project entry through judging to final tallying in one place.
home.hero.title: Judging software for hackathons
home.hero.body: Each judge is issued their own private link. They score every criterion during the demo pitches. The leaderboard is complete at the end.
home.how.title: How it works
home.how.body: Setting up hackathon judging takes about ten minutes. The math runs itself once the demos start.
home.how.1.title: Create the hackathon
home.how.1.body: Add the teams or projects and decide how many judges will score them.
home.how.2.title: Define the scoring criteria
home.how.2.body: Give each criterion its own maximum, or weight them as percentages.
home.how.3.title: Send judges their private links
home.how.3.body: Each judge gets a unique link. No account, no install, any device.
home.how.4.title: Judges score during the demos
home.how.4.body: Scores save as they type. Optionally drop the highest and lowest score per project.
home.how.5.title: Display the live leaderboard
home.how.5.body: Open the public leaderboard URL on the demo-room screen in full screen.
home.how.6.title: Announce the winners and export
home.how.6.body: Export the per-judge breakdown for sponsors, students and your own records.
home.features.title: Built for the demo room
home.features.criteria.title: Per-criterion points
home.features.criteria.body: Each criterion carries its own maximum, so technical execution can count for more than presentation.
home.features.links.title: Private judge links
home.features.links.body: Judges cannot see each other's scores in progress, which stops anchoring bias.
home.features.board.title: Live leaderboard
home.features.board.body: A public URL the demo-room screen can open full screen. Updates without a manual refresh.
home.features.drop.title: Drop high/low scores
home.features.drop.body: Remove sponsor-judge and first-time-judge outliers automatically, with one toggle.
home.features.devices.title: Works on any device
home.features.devices.body: Sponsors judge on phones, students on laptops, mentors on tablets. Nothing to install.
home.features.export.title: Per-judge breakdown export
home.features.export.body: Keep the per-judge detail and export it as CSV for any disputed placement.

judge.help.title: How to score
judge.help.body: Enter a score for each criterion, up to the maximum shown next to each field. Decimal values are accepted. Scores are saved automatically as you type. You can also add feedback notes for each entry below the scores. When you have finished scoring all entries, click Mark as complete at the bottom — this is required to submit your scores.

sys.storage.title: Storage and durability
sys.storage.body: Back up this one directory and nothing is lost: it holds the database, its write-ahead log and the session key.
sys.storage.ephemeralWarning: The session key could not be written to disk, so a random one is in use and every restart signs organizers out. Set SESSION_SECRET to fix this. Accounts and competitions themselves are unaffected.
